description: Registered exceptions to the Effect rules of mono-web. Each suppression of an Effect rule (a disable comment of effecttsgo/*, effect/*, or anti-slop-effect/*, an oxlint-effect-plugin allow directive, @effect-expect-leaking, @effect-leakable-service, @effect-diagnostics) and each non-native substitute names its entry id in a comment at the site. `just exceptions` checks every entry against its sites, its owner, and the versions that package.json pins. .agents/skills/effect-house/references/exceptions.md describes the fields and how an entry is added and retired.

exceptions.reason: The native web handler serves the built router through HttpEffect.toWebHandler. toWebHandler answers every failure cause with a response, so the handler never fails.
exceptions.missingCapability: HttpRouter.asHttpEffect() types the failure of the built router as unknown.
nativeAlternatives: HttpRouter.toHttpEffect(appLayer) types the failure from the route layers, but it builds the router from the application layer in the caller's scope. The entry point, the legacy candidate journey, and the organization import rehearsal read the router from their ManagedRuntime, which also runs their other services, such as the workers and the identity engine of the entry point.
Handling the failure before HttpEffect.toWebHandler, for example with Effect.catchCause, replaces the response that toWebHandler writes for each cause.
verification: Every journey that starts the backend entry point serves its requests through this handler, for example `just e2e interview-response`.
`just rehearsal organization-import` serves its native API through this handler.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: HttpRouter.asHttpEffect() types its failure, or the callers build their handler with HttpRouter.toHttpEffect. Then remove the suppression.

exceptions.reason: Each failure tag maps to the problem type that its case returns, and other failures pass through unchanged, so the type check of an endpoint still sees an unmapped failure.
exceptions.missingCapability: TypeScript cannot index the generic Cases record by the failure tag inside Effect.mapError, so it does not infer the mapped failure union MappedFailure<E, Failure, Cases>.
nativeAlternatives: Effect.mapError without the assertion types the failure as E | Problem, which loses the problem type of each tag that the endpoint checks rely on.
Effect.catchTags takes Effect-returning handlers keyed by literal tags. Deriving them from the generic cases record needs the same assertion.
Effect.catchIf with a type guard, as unreachable in the same file does, narrows one known failure, not a record of cases.
verification: `just check-types` checks every RPC whose problems a mapper produces.
The RPC tests of the contexts decode the answered problems through the contract's error schemas, for example `apps/backend/src/content/rpc.test.ts`.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: TypeScript infers the mapped failure union from the generic cases record. Then remove the assertion and the suppression.

exceptions.reason: The snapshot reader must refuse a symbolic link that replaces a checked path between the check and the open, so it opens each file with O_NOFOLLOW.
exceptions.missingCapability: Effect FileSystem.open takes an OpenFlag string, such as "r", which has no no-follow form, so it cannot refuse a symbolic link when it opens the file.
nativeAlternatives: FileSystem.stat or FileSystem.readLink before FileSystem.open: a symbolic link can replace the path between the check and the open.
FileSystem.realPath and a check that the result stays under the root: the same race between the check and the open.
verification: `apps/backend/src/receipt/import-snapshot.test.ts` rejects traversal, missing bytes, and a symbolic link out of the root before it imports private files.
No test replaces a path between the check and the open; review verifies the O_NOFOLLOW open.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: Effect FileSystem.open can refuse a symbolic link, for example with a no-follow flag. Then open through FileSystem and remove the node:fs/promises import.

exceptions.reason: Playwright serializes the page.evaluate callback and runs it in the browser page, where window is the global of the page. The journey removes the trailing slash from the page URL without a new request.
exceptions.missingCapability: effect/no-cross-runtime judges code by the platform of its module, which oxlint.config.ts declares node for the journey specs. It cannot see that Playwright runs a page.evaluate callback in the browser.
nativeAlternatives: page.goto with the canonical URL loads the page again, which reads the invitation again. history.replaceState changes the URL without a request.
A module that oxlint.config.ts declares platform browser can hold the callback, because Playwright serializes only the source of a self-contained function. This needs a group in oxlint.config.ts.
verification: `just e2e interview-response` runs the spec in the hosted journey matrix.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: The callback moves to a module that oxlint.config.ts declares platform browser, or effect/no-cross-runtime recognizes Playwright page callbacks. Then remove the suppressions.

exceptions.reason: Session reads and revocations run in the ambient Database transaction of the caller, so every IdentitySnapshot operation requires Database.
exceptions.missingCapability: None in Effect: the requirement is part of the contract. effecttsgo/leaking-requirements reports a service whose operations all require the same service, and the expectation accepts Database only.
nativeAlternatives: Resolving Database when the layer is built, as the rule suggests: the operations would then use the Database of the layer, not the Database of the caller whose transaction they join.
verification: `packages/database/src/auth-live.test.ts` runs the session reads against a disposable cluster (AUTH_TEST_PG_URL).
`just e2e identity` signs in, reads, and revokes sessions through the backend.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: No caller runs these operations inside its own transaction. Then resolve Database when the layer is built and remove the expectation.

exceptions.reason: The capability topology gives ContentManagement no layer dependency, so the composition root supplies Organization to every operation.
exceptions.missingCapability: None in Effect: the requirement follows the capability topology. The backend builds ContentManagementLive from the database layer alone and provides Organization per request with HttpRouter.provideRequest.
nativeAlternatives: Resolving Organization when the ContentManagement layer is built, as the rule suggests: this adds the layer dependency that the capability topology leaves out.
verification: `apps/backend/src/content/http.test.ts` answers the content operations with the problems that they declare.
`just e2e content-publication` publishes articles through the backend.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: The capability topology lets ContentManagement depend on Organization. Then provide Organization when the layer is built and remove the expectation.

exceptions.reason: The cohort reader must refuse a symbolic link that replaces the private cohort file between the check and the open, so it opens the file with O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW and checks the type, size, mode, and owner of the opened file.
exceptions.missingCapability: Effect FileSystem.open takes an OpenFlag string, such as "r", which has no no-follow form, so it cannot refuse a symbolic link when it opens the file.
nativeAlternatives: FileSystem.stat or FileSystem.readLink before FileSystem.open: a symbolic link can replace the path between the check and the open.
FileSystem.readFileString after a check of the path: the same race, and the read cannot check the file that it opened.
verification: `just rehearsal current-assignment` writes a private cohort file and imports it through `tools/verification/current-assignment-cohort-cli.ts`, which reads it with readPrivateCohortJson.
No test replaces the path with a symbolic link or widens its mode; review verifies the O_NOFOLLOW open and the checks of the opened file.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: Effect FileSystem.open can refuse a symbolic link, for example with a no-follow flag. Then open through FileSystem and remove the node:fs/promises import.

exceptions.reason: The recommendation probe reports its fixture check, its gate milestones, its returning stages, its result, and its failure evidence as lines on standard output and standard error, which the operator reads. Each line is bounded, and the failure evidence is redacted.
exceptions.missingCapability: None in Effect: Console of effect writes the same lines, but only inside an Effect program. The probe is a script of top-level Promise code with no Effect runtime at its entry point.
nativeAlternatives: Console.log and Console.error of effect, each run with Effect.runSync at its site: that runs programs outside an owned entry point, which FX003 and effect/no-premature-execution reject.
One Effect program that the entry point of the probe runs: a rewrite of the whole probe, which is the retirement path.
verification: The hosted journey matrix runs the probe as `just e2e recommendation-applicant-progress`, `recommendation-co-interviewer`, `recommendation-correction`, and `recommendation-returning`.
The plugin accepts a directive only when it names no-ambient-console alone with a nonempty `dev only:` reason, and it reports broad, unreasoned, and unused directives.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: The probe becomes an Effect program that its entry point runs, and it writes through Console of effect. Then remove the directives.

exceptions.reason: decodeSnapshot is the Schema decoder of a receipt snapshot with excess properties refused. Its callers pass fixtures and malformed rows whose static type is not JSON, such as rows with `data: unknown`, because the importer must quarantine them; its second parameter is the parse options of the decoder, not the subject of a data-last call.
exceptions.missingCapability: None in Effect. Schema.decodeUnknownSync returns `(input: unknown, options?: ParseOptions) => A`, and the rule asks for a pipeable overload of that signature, which a decoder of one subject has no use for.
nativeAlternatives: A one-parameter wrapper typed `(input: Schema.Json)`, as the domain decoders use: the receipt import rehearsal and the snapshot test pass rows whose data is `unknown` or `Json | undefined`, so each caller would have to change its fixture types.
A one-parameter wrapper typed `(input: unknown)`: `anti-slop/no-unknown-parameters` rejects it.
Exporting ReceiptSnapshot and decoding at each call site: every caller would repeat `onExcessProperty: "error"`, a fact that one decoder should own.
`dual` from `effect/Function`: the second parameter is parse options, so a data-last form reads the options as the subject.
verification: `apps/backend/src/receipt/import-snapshot.test.ts` decodes a synthetic snapshot through it.

`just rehearsal receipt-import` (`tools/verification/receipt-import-rehearsal.ts`) decodes its manifest through it, and `tools/e2e/run-legacy-receipt-rehearsal.ts` checks that it rejects another snapshot kind.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: The callers decode JSON-typed input, or the rule exempts Schema decoders. Then give decodeSnapshot a one-parameter form and remove the suppression.

exceptions.reason: Vocs loads `vocs.config.ts` under Node and calls its sidebar builders and remark plugins synchronously: `site.ts` lists the specifications and reads each page's first heading while the configuration evaluates, and the remark plugin checks whether a linked repository path exists while it transforms a page.
exceptions.missingCapability: Effect FileSystem has no synchronous backend: the Node and Bun layers implement every operation asynchronously, so Effect.runSync cannot read a directory or a file.
nativeAlternatives: Effect.runSync with the FileSystem service: fails with an asynchronous operation.

An asynchronous configuration that runs an Effect program with Effect.runPromise: Vite awaits a Promise default export, but the production branch of the Vocs 2.10.0 resolver spreads the default export without awaiting it, and the remark plugin would run a program outside a composition root in every transform.
Precomputing titles and link targets in `scripts/sync-pages.ts`: the remark plugin resolves links to any repository path, and `vocs dev` would read stale titles until the script ran again.
verification: `bun run --cwd apps/docs build` renders every published page, builds the sidebar from `site.ts`, and fails on a dead link that the remark plugin leaves unchanged.
The Docs workflow runs that build.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: Vocs awaits an asynchronous configuration in every branch and remark plugins may run Effect programs through a runtime bridge, or Effect gains a synchronous FileSystem. Then read through FileSystem and remove the suppressions.
